```
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

content.content:
1	---
2	title: "The Export Queue"
3	description: "Write exports behind the editor, one at a time, while you keep working, and follow, cancel or reveal each one from a single window."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The Export Queue writes the same file as **Export…** without making you wait for it. Jobs run one at a time behind the editor while you keep working.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Window ▸ Export Queue"
13	  where="Export sheet ▸ Add to Queue"
14	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Add to Queue
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Set up the file in the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
22	
23	2. Choose **Add to Queue**. It's available whenever **Export…** is.
24	
25	3. Name the file in the save panel and choose **Save**. This is the same panel **Export…** opens.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	The **Export Queue** window then opens on its own, with the job in it. Your settings are remembered as the last choice, as they are for **Export…**.
30	
31	Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** no progress sheet is in the way. You can start playback again and go on editing while the job runs.
32	
33	## The Export Queue window
34	
35	Choose **Window ▸ Export Queue** to open it at any time. It has no keyboard shortcut.
36	
37	The window lists every queued, running and finished export. Jobs run one at a time, in the order they were added, unless a job has to [wait for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). Closing the window stops nothing. Open it again and the jobs are where they'd got to.
38	
39	The line at the bottom counts the jobs, for example "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished". With nothing in the list, the window reads "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."
40	
41	The list isn't saved. It starts empty each time you open Frame Job.
42	
43	## Rows and their states
44	
45	Each row shows the file's name and where the job has got to.
46	
47	| The row says | What it means | Button |
48	| --- | --- | --- |
49	| `Waiting` | Queued behind the running job. | **Cancel** |
50	| `Waiting for memory: …` | An AV1 or VP9 job [waiting for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). | **Cancel** |
51	| `Writing · 42 %` | The job is running, with a progress bar beside it. It can stay at `Writing · 0 %` while the job [waits for what it needs](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs). | **Cancel** |
52	| `Measuring loudness… · 12 %` | The job is measuring the mix before it writes. | **Cancel** |
53	| `Stopping…` | You cancelled the job and it hasn't stopped yet. | **Cancel** |
54	| `Exported “Board.mp4”.` | The file landed. Any stems, graphic warnings and cursor warnings are counted after the name, then come the [loudness figures](/export/progress-and-report/). | **Show**, **Remove** |
55	| `Overwritten by a later export to the same file.` | The job finished, but a later job has since started writing to the same path. | **Remove** |
56	| `Cancelled.` | You stopped it while it ran. | **Remove** |
57	| `Cancelled before it started.` | You stopped it while it waited. | **Remove** |
58	| The reason it failed | The job stopped with an error. | **Remove** |
59	
60	Hold the pointer over a row for its tooltip: the full path, the container, the size and the frame rate, then the whole memory sentence while a job waits for memory, then each graphic and cursor warning.
61	
62	| Button | What it does |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| **Cancel** | Stops that job and removes its half-written file. A waiting job is cancelled before it starts. |
65	| **Remove** | Takes a finished row out of the list. The file stays where it is. |
66	| **Show** | Reveals the finished file in the Finder. If the file has since been moved or deleted, Frame Job beeps. |
67	
68	## Clear Finished and Cancel All
69	
70	**Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row and leaves the queue running. It's dimmed when there's nothing to clear, and it deletes no files.
71	
72	**Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one. It's dimmed when nothing is running or waiting.
73	
74	A cancelled job's half-written file is removed. A job that failed leaves on disk whatever it had written, unless its message says no file was written.
75	
76	## A queued job's snapshot
77	
78	A job holds the timeline as it was when you chose **Save** in the save panel, including its media files, reversed clips, graphics, chapters and any timecode burn-in.
79	
80	Edits, undos and relinks made afterwards don't change what it writes, and neither does closing the document. You can queue one version, go on cutting, and queue another.
81	
82	## Quit with jobs in the queue
83	
84	Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first, after Frame Job has asked about any unsaved documents.
85	
86	The alert reads "An export is still being written." and names the running file, for example "“Board.mp4” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting. Quitting now stops it and deletes the partly written file."
87	
88	- **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue, deletes the partly written file and quits.
89	- **Cancel** keeps Frame Job open and the queue running.
90	
91	:::caution
92	Only the queue is guarded this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel that export first.
93	:::
94	
95	## The encoder memory wait
96	
97	AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, and they use a lot of memory.
98	
99	| Format | At 1080p | At 4K |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM), depending on [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) | About 1.2–2.4 GB | About 4.4–8.1 GB |
102	| VP9 (WebM) | About 0.4–0.5 GB | About 1.1–1.6 GB |
103	| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | About 0.7 GB | About 2.2 GB |
104	
105	All the AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may hold up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. On a 16 GB Mac that's 4.0 GB.
106	
107	A queued AV1 or VP9 job starts only if it fits in that quarter with what's already running. The queue itself runs one job at a time, so what holds a job back is an AV1 or VP9 export running behind an **Export…** progress sheet.
108	
109	- When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large.
110	- While a job waits, a later job that fits runs first, and so does any job in a format the Mac encodes itself, such as H.264 or ProRes.
111	- An **Export…** sheet never waits. It's counted and starts straight away, so several sheets at once can go past the quarter.
112	
113	The row's status is one line, so the sentence usually ends in "…" before its figures. The tooltip ends with all of it: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB."
114	
115	The figures are measured, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.
116	
117	## Good to know
118	
119	- **Export…** doesn't join the queue. It writes straight away behind its [own progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/), and it can run while a queued job runs.
120	- Two jobs can name the same file. The save panel asks about replacing a file only if it's already on disk, so two quick **Add to Queue** choices with one name may not ask at all. The later job replaces the file as it starts writing, whether or not it goes on to finish, and the earlier row stops offering **Show**.
121	
122	## With an agent
123	
124	An agent's `export` always goes through the queue, never a progress sheet. Its job is a row like any other, but the window doesn't open on its own. `export_status` reads that row and `cancel_export` is its **Cancel**. An agent can follow and stop only the jobs it started. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
125	
126	## Related
127	
128	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
129	- [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/)
130	- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
131	- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
132

1	---
2	title: "Save Frame"
3	description: "Save the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC, drawn at full size the way an export draws it."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Save Frame writes the frame under the playhead to a still image: a thumbnail, a poster frame or a picture for a document.
10	
11	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Save Frame…" keys="⌥⌘E" tools="render_frame" />
12	
13	## Save a frame
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Move the playhead to the frame.
18	
19	2. Choose **File ▸ Save Frame…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>. It's greyed out while the timeline is empty.
20	
21	3. Pick a **Format:** and a place. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` in place of `:`, such as `Board 00-00-12-05.png`.
22	
23	4. Choose **Save**.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	The frame is the one the playhead was on when you opened the panel. When the save works, nothing else appears. The file is where you put it.
28	
29	If it doesn't work, an alert says why:
30	
31	| The alert says | What it means |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing." | Frame Job couldn't draw a frame at that time. |
34	| "Could not write PNG to … The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it." | The folder is missing, or Frame Job can't write into it. |
35	| "Could not write HEIC to … This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format." | This Mac has no encoder for the format. |
36	
37	## PNG, JPEG or HEIC
38	
39	| **Format:** | File | Transparency | Depth | Compression |
40	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
41	| **PNG** | `.png` | Kept | 8-bit, or 16-bit for a [deep frame](#deep-and-hdr-frames) | Lossless |
42	| **JPEG** | `.jpg` | None. A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. | Always 8-bit | 90 % quality |
43	| **HEIC** | `.heic` | Kept | 8-bit, or 10-bit for a deep frame | 90 % quality |
44	
45	The popup opens on **PNG** every time and doesn't remember your last choice. A line under it says what the chosen format does with transparency, such as "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
46	
47	Choosing a format changes the extension in the file name and keeps a name you've typed. Only `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` and `.heic` count as extensions, so `Board v1.2` keeps its `.2` and becomes `Board v1.2.jpg`.
48	
49	## Drawn the way an export draws it
50	
51	The frame is drawn the way an [export](/export/what-an-export-includes/) draws it, at the canvas's full size.
52	
53	Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version and Show Selection never change it. It never carries a timecode burn-in, even if you use one on your exports.
54	
55	## Inside a nest
56	
57	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the saved frame is the picture the canvas is showing: the nest's own, at the nest's size and the nest's time. The timecode in the suggested name is the nest's too. Save Frame is greyed out in an empty nest, however full the timeline is.
58	
59	This is the opposite of an export, which always writes the whole timeline.
60	
61	## Deep and HDR frames
62	
63	Most frames are saved at 8 bits a channel and labelled BT.709. These are saved with more:
64	
65	- **A deep frame.** A frame showing a still deeper than 8 bits, or a 10-bit VP9 clip, is saved as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, still labelled BT.709. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip is saved deep too, when every video track in the timeline is that deep.
66	- **An [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/).** Every PNG and HEIC keeps the HLG picture, as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG.
67	
68	JPEG is always 8-bit. In an HDR project a JPEG is the project's [SDR version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), labelled BT.709.
69	
70	See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/) for how depth runs through the rest of the app.
71	
72	## Waiting for masks
73	
74	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, which are made on this Mac. Past that, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the clip's file, for example "speech.mov drawn whole: the person masks were not ready within 30 seconds."
75	
76	Save the frame again once the clip's **Status** row shows the masks are done. An export never does this: it [waits as long as the masks take](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs).
77	
78	## Good to know
79	
80	A graphic that fails draws its error card in the saved frame, and a clip whose cursor file can't be read is drawn without its cursor. Save Frame doesn't warn you about either, so look at the picture.
81	
82	## The same still for an agent
83	
84	`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame for the same frame and format. It answers with the picture itself as well as a file, and with no path it writes a temporary PNG and names it.
85	
86	It also reports what Save Frame keeps quiet: when a graphic in the frame warned or failed it names the graphic, its frame and the message, and it names a cursor file it couldn't read. Like Save Frame, it waits 30 seconds for masks and says which clip it drew whole. An agent can ask for more than the menu offers, such as a timecode burn-in, an ungraded picture or scope measurements. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
87	
88	## Related
89	
90	- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
91	- [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/)
92	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
93

1	---
2	title: "Transparent exports"
3	description: "Export a title or overlay with a transparent background, and choose the format that keeps it for the place it's going."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A transparent canvas lets you export a title, a lower third or an overlay that sits on top of something else. Only four formats keep the transparency, so the format is the choice that matters.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where={['Document tab ▸ Appearance ▸ Background', 'Export sheet ▸ Format']}
13	  tools={['set_canvas', 'export']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Export with transparency
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. [Make the canvas background transparent](/projects/background-and-timecode/#make-the-background-transparent) in the Document tab.
21	
22	2. Open the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) and pick a format that keeps transparency. The sheet's [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`, for example `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`.
23	
24	3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.
25	
26	</Steps>
27	
28	## Which formats keep transparency
29	
30	A transparent canvas stays transparent in four formats:
31	
32	- **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**
33	- **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**
34	- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)**
35	- **Animated PNG**
36	
37	Every other format composites the picture onto black. **Animated GIF** isn't one of the four: a GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partly transparent survives it.
38	
39	For a single frame, [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#png-jpeg-or-heic) keeps transparency in PNG and HEIC, and JPEG flattens onto black.
40	
41	## The Transparency note
42	
43	While the canvas background isn't fully opaque, the **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) says which formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats."
44	
45	The note names the formats when there are one or two, and counts them from three up. In a document with no length it reads "Transparent — needs an alpha format."
46	
47	## Which transparent movie to send
48	
49	| Send | For | Good to know |
50	| --- | --- | --- |
51	| **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** | The web: a `<video>` in a page, in Chrome and Firefox | Only a player that decodes VP9 with libvpx shows the transparency. Others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque. Safari hasn't been confirmed to show it. |
52	| **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)** | Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps | The transparent movie for Apple's players. |
53	| **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** | Another editor | The master. |
54	
55	To bring a transparent clip back into Frame Job, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha. A VP9 with Alpha file keeps its picture when you import it but loses its transparency, showing black where it was transparent.
56	
57	## Straight alpha
58	
59	The colour in all three transparent movies is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.
60	
61	Frame Job also fills the transparent pixels just outside the picture, up to 4 pixels out, with the colour of the edge beside them. Without that, a codec that averages colour across pixels would darken the edge. This is automatic, and there's nothing to set.
62	
63	## The same-shape rule
64	
65	ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha won't write a frame of a different shape from the canvas. Fitting the picture into another shape would pad it, and the padding destroys the alpha channel.
66	
67	Every row in the [**Size:** popup](/export/size/) has the canvas's shape, so this only happens with a **Custom…** size. Scaling is fine, larger or smaller, as long as the proportions hold, and a size within a pixel of the canvas's shape is written.
68	
69	After the save panel, the export stops with a message naming both sizes: "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape. This canvas is 1920 × 1080 and 1000 × 1000 is a different shape, so the picture would be padded and the padding loses the alpha channel. Export at 1920 × 1080, at one of the sizes in the popup, or at any size with the same proportions."
70	
71	## Good to know
72	
73	HEVC with Alpha, VP9 with Alpha and Animated PNG are 8-bit. In an [HDR project](/hdr/export-hdr/) they write the SDR version, so use ProRes 4444 to keep both HDR and transparency.
74	
75	## Related
76	
77	- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
78	- [ProRes](/export/prores/)
79	- [H.264 and HEVC](/export/h264-and-hevc/)
80	- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
81	- [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/)

1	---
2	title: "Chapters"
3	description: "Turn chapter markers into chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, and see how a range export treats them."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Chapters let someone jump through a long video in their player. In Frame Job they come from the markers you've ticked as chapters, with nothing to set on the export sheet.
9	
10	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Markers ▸ Chapter" tools={['export', 'add_marker', 'set_marker']} />
11	
12	## Chapters in exports
13	
14	[Mark a chapter](/timeline/markers/#make-a-chapter) on the timeline, then export to any format that writes an MP4, MOV, M4A or WebM file. Chapter markers become the file's chapters, in time order.
15	
16	- **Names.** A chapter takes its marker's name. An unnamed marker becomes "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on, counted over the chapter markers only, so removing a plain marker never renumbers them. A name of only spaces counts as unnamed.
17	- **Lengths.** Each chapter runs to the next one, and the last runs to the end of the file. Time before the first chapter marker belongs to no chapter, so put a marker on the first frame if you want the file to open in one.
18	- **Queued jobs.** A job writes the chapters the timeline had when you confirmed it, whatever you do to the markers afterwards. See [A queued job's snapshot](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot).
19	
20	WAV, AIFF, Animated GIF and Animated PNG files have no chapters. Neither do [stems](/export/stems/): only the mix carries them.
21	
22	## Chapters in a range export
23	
24	An [export of a range](/export/range/) keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file. The chapter already running when the range starts opens the file, and a chapter starting at or after the range's end is left out.
25	
26	Say the timeline has chapters at 0:00, 1:00 and 3:00, named Intro, Demo and Outro, and you export from 2:00 to 4:00. The file has two chapters: Demo at 0:00 and Outro at 1:00.
27	
28	An unnamed chapter keeps its number from the whole timeline, so the third chapter marker is still "Chapter 3" in a file that holds only two.
29	
30	## Related
31	
32	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
33	- [Export a range](/export/range/)
34	- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
35

1	---
2	title: "What an export includes"
3	description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />
11	
12	## The same picture and sound
13	
14	An export uses the same composition and the same compositor as the preview, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.
15	
16	View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).
17	
18	The sound has one thing the preview doesn't: the master limiter, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
19	
20	## Waiting for what it needs
21	
22	Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip.
23	
24	| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture set to Foreground) and no file is written |
27	| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
28	| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
29	| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
30	| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
31	| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |
32	
33	Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.
34	
35	While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.
36	
37	[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.
38	
39	## Missing media
40	
41	A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.
42	
43	An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).
44	
45	## Graphics
46	
47	An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a module is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.
48	
49	If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.
50	
51	That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."
52	
53	## Captions
54	
55	Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).
56	
57	## Colour labels
58	
59	An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.
60	
61	## Related
62	
63	- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
64	- [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/)
65	- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
66	- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

190	    /// rate that cannot be stepped (no frame count, so no estimate rather than 0 frames).
191	    static func estimatedSeconds(for settings: ExportSettings) -> Double? {
192	        guard let key = ExportEncoderKey(settings: settings), let entry = time[key],
193	            let frames = settings.sequenceFrameCount

195	            return nil
196	        }
197	        return entry.setupSeconds
198	            + Double(frames) * entry.perFrame.value(pixels: settings.width * settings.height)

202	    /// minutes under an hour.

204	        if s < 60 { return "about \(max(5, Int((s / 5).rounded()) * 5)) s" }

217	/// The app-wide account of the bundled-encoder exports running now (spec §11 CX-18): the
218	/// Export Queue's job and every Export… progress sheet's, each booked from just before its
219	/// exporter starts to its finish, at the resident peak `ExportEncoderCosts.memory` measured
220	/// for its key and size.
221	///
222	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
223	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
224	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
225	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
226	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
227	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.
228	///
229	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
230	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when
231	/// nothing is booked — one export always runs, however large — or when the booked costs and
232	/// its own fit.
233	///
234	/// Main thread only, like the queue and the sheets that book into it, and AppKit-free so a
235	/// probe compiles it headless (`tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`).
236	final class ExportEncoderLedger {
237	    /// The app's one ledger. The queue observes it and the sheets book into it.
238	    static let shared = ExportEncoderLedger()
239	
240	    /// Posted after a booking is added or removed, with the ledger as the `object`. The
241	    /// queue re-runs `start()` on it, so a held job launches when a booking ends.
242	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
243	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportEncoderLedgerDidChange")
244	
245	    /// The Mac's memory the budget is a share of — `ProcessInfo`'s, which a probe sets to
246	    /// ask what a Mac of another size would admit.
247	    var physicalMemory: UInt64
248	
249	    private var entries: [(token: UInt64, cost: UInt64)] = []
250	    private var nextToken: UInt64 = 1
251	
252	    init(physicalMemory: UInt64 = ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory) {
253	        self.physicalMemory = physicalMemory
254	    }
255	
256	    /// What bundled-encoder exports may hold together, in bytes.
257	    var budget: UInt64 { Self.budget(physicalMemory: physicalMemory) }
258	
259	    /// Each running booking's cost, in booking order.
260	    var runningCosts: [UInt64] { entries.map(\.cost) }
261	
262	    // MARK: - The rule
263	
264	    /// A quarter of physical memory (CX-18 (3)).
265	    static func budget(physicalMemory: UInt64) -> UInt64 { physicalMemory / 4 }
266	
267	    /// Whether a job costing `cost` may start beside `running`: always when nothing runs,
268	    /// else when the sum fits `budget` (CX-18 (5)).
269	    static func admits(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> Bool {
270	        guard !running.isEmpty else { return true }
271	        let (inUse, over) = running.reduce((UInt64(0), false)) { sum, next in
272	            let added = sum.0.addingReportingOverflow(next)
273	            return (added.partialValue, sum.1 || added.overflow)
274	        }
275	        let total = inUse.addingReportingOverflow(cost)
276	        return !over && !total.overflow && total.partialValue <= budget
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The held job's sentence: what runs, what the Mac allows, what this one needs.
280	    static func waitingSentence(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> String {
281	        let inUse = running.reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 &+ $1 }
282	        return "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about "
283	            + "\(gigabytes(inUse)) of the \(gigabytes(budget)) this Mac allows them, and this "
284	            + "one needs about \(gigabytes(cost))."
285	    }
286	
287	    private static func gigabytes(_ bytes: UInt64) -> String {
288	        String(format: "%.1f GB", Double(bytes) / 1_073_741_824)
289	    }
290	
291	    // MARK: - Asking
292	
293	    /// Whether `settings` may start now, leaving out the booking `token` (the queue's own
294	    /// running job, which a waiting job is behind anyway). True for an AVFoundation row.
295	    func admits(_ settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> Bool {
296	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return true }
297	        return Self.admits(
298	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
299	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
300	    }
301	
302	    /// The held sentence for `settings`, or nil when it is admitted.
303	    func waitingSentence(for settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> String? {
304	        guard !admits(settings, ignoring: token) else { return nil }
305	        return Self.waitingSentence(
306	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
307	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
308	    }
309	
310	    private func costs(ignoring token: UInt64?) -> [UInt64] {
311	        entries.filter { $0.token != token }.map(\.cost)
312	    }
313	
314	    // MARK: - Booking
315	
316	    /// Books an export about to start and answers its token, or nil — booking nothing —
317	    /// for an AVFoundation row. Called BEFORE `Exporter.export`, whose early refusals finish
318	    /// synchronously inside it.
319	    func begin(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> UInt64? {
320	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return nil }
321	        let token = nextToken
322	        nextToken += 1
323	        entries.append(
324	            (token, ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget)))
325	        post()
326	        return token
327	    }
328	
329	    /// Ends a booking. A nil or unknown token is a no-op; a removal posts, and the queue's
330	    /// observer may launch its next job — and book it — inside this call, which is why a
331	    /// caller clears its own token BEFORE calling this.
332	    func end(_ token: UInt64?) {
333	        guard let token, let index = entries.firstIndex(where: { $0.token == token }) else {
334	            return
335	        }
336	        entries.remove(at: index)
337	        post()
338	    }
339	
340	    private func post() {
341	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
342	    }
343	}

506	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
507	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of

511	    // MARK: - Commit
512	
513	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
514	        dismiss(self)
515	    }
516	
517	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
518	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
519	        commit(queue: false)
520	    }
521	
522	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
523	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
524	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
525	        commit(queue: true)
526	    }

528	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
529	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
530	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
531	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
532	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
533	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
534	    /// one held until its turn.
535	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
536	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
537	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
538	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
539	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
540	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
541	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
542	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
543	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
544	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
545	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
546	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
547	              let window = editor.view.window
548	        else {
549	            NSSound.beep()
550	            return
551	        }
552	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
553	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
554	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
555	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
556	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
557	        let options = recipeOptions
558	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
559	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
560	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
561	        // buttons record it.
562	        currentChoice.remember()
563	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
564	        dismiss(self)

567	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
568	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true

570	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
571	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
572	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
573	        }
574	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
575	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
576	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in

580	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
581	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
582	            if queue {

592	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
593	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)

599	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)

603	        return stem + "." + Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)

14	/// larger of C6a's (C5's) single run and C6b's peaks, its source naming the run that won.

19	/// What a cost is keyed by: the row, the AV1 speed, and the bit depth the encoder runs at.
20	struct ExportEncoderKey: Hashable {
21	    /// `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm`.
22	    let preset: String
23	    /// The AV1 rows' speed (`settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced`); nil on every other row.

25	    /// 10 on `svt_av1` (CX-14: always 10-bit); on `libvpx` 10 for `hlg`/`pq` (Profile 2,
26	    /// CX-16 (3)), else 8.
27	    let bits: Int

29	    init(preset: String, speed: EncoderSpeed?, bits: Int) {
30	        self.preset = preset
31	        self.speed = speed
32	        self.bits = bits
33	    }

35	    /// The key of an export's settings; nil for an AVFoundation row (no `writer`).
36	    init?(settings: ExportSettings) {
37	        guard let writer = settings.writer else { return nil }
38	        let av1 = writer == "svt_av1"
39	        let deep = settings.dynamicRange == .hlg || settings.dynamicRange == .pq
40	        self.init(
41	            preset: settings.preset, speed: av1 ? settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced : nil,
42	            bits: av1 || deep ? 10 : 8)

181	    /// What `settings` books in the ledger: 0 for an AVFoundation row, the whole `budget`

217	/// The app-wide account of the bundled-encoder exports running now (spec §11 CX-18): the
218	/// Export Queue's job and every Export… progress sheet's, each booked from just before its
219	/// exporter starts to its finish, at the resident peak `ExportEncoderCosts.memory` measured
220	/// for its key and size.
221	///
222	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
223	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
224	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
225	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
226	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
227	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.
228	///
229	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
230	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when

extension Exporter {

    /// Why an export stopped. Every case is reported through `completion` —
    /// nothing here throws at the caller and nothing crashes.
    enum ExportError: LocalizedError {
        /// The core could not produce a composition plan for this project.
        case noPlan
        /// Nothing to write: no video and no audio track in the plan. Reached
        /// by an empty timeline AND by one holding only text, shapes and
        /// images, which need no composition track (spec §7.2) — so the
        /// message has to name the second case, which is the surprising one.
        case emptyTimeline

        /// unknown codec name, one `AVAssetWriter` refuses an input for, or
        /// one whose encoder is not found when the write starts
        /// (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`). Carries the preset id when the core
        /// gave one, else the codec.
        case presetUnavailable(String)
        /// The settings named a container this build cannot map to a file
        /// type.
        case fileTypeUnsupported(String)

        /// from the canvas, which cannot be written correctly and so is not
        /// written at all (road map 2, phase 7b). Carries the canvas and the
        /// size the core resolved, in that order.

143	    /// What a finished write becomes when the reason it failed is that this
144	    /// Mac has no encoder for the row (spec §11 G-33 (e)): the preset's own
145	    /// sentence, and no file.

149	    /// alike: `canApply` is true, the input constructs, `canAdd` is true, and
150	    /// `startWriting()` then fails with `AVFoundationErrorDomain` −11834
151	    /// ("Cannot Encode"), leaving a 0-byte file at the destination. So it is
152	    /// mapped here, where `startWriting` hears the pipeline: exactly that
153	    /// domain and code become `.presetUnavailable` with the preset's name and
154	    /// the file is removed, and every other result is returned as it came.
155	    static func encoderOutcome(
156	        _ result: Result<URL, any Error>, settings: ExportSettings, destination: URL
157	    ) -> Result<URL, any Error> {
158	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else { return result }
159	        let reason = error as NSError

161	            reason.code == AVError.Code.encoderNotFound.rawValue
162	        else { return result }

184	    private static let maskOwnersLock = NSLock()
185	    /// An export's recipe key → its lane owner, made at its first want.

188	    /// The lane owner of the export writing under `key`, made on first use.
189	    private static func maskOwner(for key: Int) -> Int {
190	        maskOwnersLock.lock()
191	        defer { maskOwnersLock.unlock() }
192	        if let owner = maskOwners[key] { return owner }

198	    /// Blocks until every mask the export's range draws is cached (CO-22 (e)): the windows of

206	        plan: CompositionPlan, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, key: Int,
207	        cancelled: @escaping () -> Bool
208	    ) throws {
209	        guard let project = RecipeSource.shared.project(for: key) else { return }
210	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
211	        let range = settings.start..<(settings.start + max(settings.duration, 0))

213	            + CutoutWants.imageWindows(snapshot: snapshot, range: range)
214	        guard let first = windows.first(where: { urls[$0.media] != nil }) else { return }

217	        }
218	        guard let cacheDir = ReverseSource.shared.resolution(for: key).cache else {
219	            throw ExportError.cutoutFailed(

222	        }
223	        let owner = maskOwner(for: key)
224	        var landings = 0
225	        while true {
226	            let (requests, failures) = CutoutWants.wants(
227	                windows: windows, snapshot: snapshot, urls: urls, cacheDir: cacheDir)
228	            if let failure = failures.first {
229	                let kind = windows.first { $0.clip == failure.clip }?.kind ?? .masks

252	                    return false

271	    /// A media's masks of one kind: the frame wait's stamps and uncovered set are keyed by it.
272	    private struct MaskKey: Hashable {
273	        let kind: AnalysisKind
274	        let media: UInt32
275	    }

277	    /// Waits up to `limit` for the masks the recipe at `t` draws (CO-22 (f)) under a fresh owner,
278	    /// polling the store every `AnalysisLane.pollInterval` until each is covered, one of its
279	    /// requests failed, or the limit; answers the clips drawn uncut, ascending — an unreadable
280	    /// media's at once, every one with no cache folder. A cut picture's masks are waited for by
281	    /// their kind beside the movies' (CO-106). Never main: it blocks.
282	    static func waitForFrameMasks(
283	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], key: Int, at t: Ticks,
284	        options: RecipeOptions, limit: TimeInterval
285	    ) -> [UInt32] {
286	        let windows = CutoutWants.frameWindows(project: project, at: t, options: options)
287	            .filter { urls[$0.media] != nil }
288	        guard !windows.isEmpty else { return [] }
289	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
290	        func clips(of keys: Set<MaskKey>) -> [UInt32] {
291	            Array(Set(windows.filter { keys.contains(MaskKey(kind: $0.kind, media: $0.media)) }
292	                .map(\.clip))).sorted()
293	        }
294	        guard let cacheDir = ReverseSource.shared.resolution(for: key).cache else {
295	            return clips(of: Set(windows.map { MaskKey(kind: $0.kind, media: $0.media) }))
296	        }
297	        var needs: [MaskKey: [ClosedRange<Int>]] = [:]
298	        for kind in Set(windows.map(\.kind)) {
299	            let byMedia = CutoutWants.needs(
300	                windows: windows.filter { $0.kind == kind }, snapshot: snapshot, urls: urls)
301	            for (media, need) in byMedia { needs[MaskKey(kind: kind, media: media)] = need }
302	        }
303	        let (requests, failures) = CutoutWants.wants(
304	            windows: windows, snapshot: snapshot, urls: urls, cacheDir: cacheDir)
305	        let unreadable = Set(failures.compactMap { failure in
306	            windows.first { $0.clip == failure.clip }.map { MaskKey(kind: $0.kind, media: $0.media) }
307	        })
308	        guard !requests.isEmpty else { return clips(of: unreadable) }
309	        // Each waited media's stamp, made once by its request; the polls only look up.
310	        var stamps: [MaskKey: AnalysisStamp] = [:]
311	        for request in requests {
312	            stamps[MaskKey(kind: request.kind, media: request.media.id)] = request.stamp
313	        }
314	        func uncovered() -> Set<MaskKey> {
315	            Set(stamps.filter { key, stamp in
316	                (needs[key] ?? []).contains {
317	                    if case .hit = AnalysisStore.lookup(
318	                        key.kind, media: key.media, stamp: stamp, need: $0, in: cacheDir)
319	                    {
320	                        return false
321	                    }
322	                    return true
323	                }
324	            }.keys)
325	        }
326	        let owner = AnalysisLane.shared.newOwner()
327	        defer { AnalysisLane.shared.release(owner: owner) }
328	        AnalysisLane.shared.want(requests, owner: owner, alive: { true }, settled: nil)
329	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
330	        CutoutWants.log(.frame, owner: owner, requests)
331	        #endif
332	        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(limit)
333	        var missing = uncovered()
334	        while !missing.isEmpty, Date() < deadline,
335	            !requests.contains(where: {
336	                if case .failed? = AnalysisLane.shared.run(of: $0)?.outcome { return true }
337	                return false
338	            })
339	        {
340	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: AnalysisLane.pollInterval)
341	            missing = uncovered()
342	        }
343	        return clips(of: missing.union(unreadable))
344	    }

103	        // one taken a moment early — so unlike the project below, the playhead
104	        // is not re-read when the panel comes back. It is left exactly as the
105	        // document holds it, which inside a nest means the nest's own time
106	        // (see the type doc): the render below is handed the same container,
107	        // so there is nothing to map, and the timecode in the name is the one

109	        let time = max(0, document.playhead)

116	        //
117	        // The base is `displayStem`: the title with the package's own
118	        // extension off and NOTHING else off. A bare `deletingPathExtension`

122	        let stem = frameStem(
123	            base: document.displayStem, at: time,
124	            canvas: document.editedProject.snapshot.canvas)

128	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false

160	        let time = ReelTime.format(t, fps: canvas.fps, frames: canvas.timecodeFrames)

167	    /// Reads the document on the main thread, composes off it, and comes back

171	    /// which is `CaptionExporter`'s rule and holds for its reason: a save

173	    /// document under it, but an agent's edit can (MCP runs on the main
174	    /// thread and a sheet does not stop it), and what the project says NOW is
175	    /// what should land. The `t` it is asked about came the other way, from
176	    /// the command — see `saveFrameCommand`, where the reason is written down.

178	    /// It is the EDITED project, which is the whole of phase 9's correction
179	    /// here and is argued in the type doc: `time` is measured in whatever
180	    /// container is open, so this is the one handle it can be spent against.
181	    /// One seam is left open by that pairing and is named rather than
182	    /// guarded: an agent's `set_scope` between the panel opening and its OK
183	    /// would spend the old container's tick in the new container. It is the
184	    /// agent-only half of a race this method already documents for edits, the
185	    /// window-modal panel rules the person out, and the honest guard for it
186	    /// would be a second opinion here about which container a tick belongs
187	    /// to — which is `ProjectDocument`'s to hold, and holding it twice is
188	    /// what made this file wrong in the first place.
189	    private func renderAndWriteFrame(
190	        from document: ProjectDocument, at time: Ticks, format: FrameWriter.Format,
191	        to url: URL, in window: NSWindow
192	    ) {
193	        let project = document.editedProject
194	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
195	        let graphics = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
196	        EditorViewController.frameGrabQueue.async { [weak self] in
197	            let result: Result<URL, Error>
198	            // `render_frame`'s expression, so the two stay one frame's bytes: a
199	            // JPEG of an HLG project is its SDR version (spec §11 HD-14 (e)).
200	            let options = RecipeOptions.none.forFrame(format, output: project.snapshot.canvas.output)
201	            // A cut-out clip waits up to 30 s for its masks (spec §11 CO-22 (f)).
202	            let rendered = Exporter.renderFrameReported(
203	                project: project, urls: urls, at: time, maxWidth: nil, options: options,
204	                graphics: graphics, keepsDepth: format.carriesDepth,
205	                cutoutWait: Exporter.frameCutoutWait)
206	            if let image = rendered.image {
207	                result = Result { try FrameWriter.writeFrame(image, as: format, to: url) }
208	            } else {
209	                result = .failure(SaveFrameError.noFrame)
210	            }
211	            let uncut = Self.uncutNote(rendered.uncut, in: project.snapshot)
212	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.frameSaved(result, in: window, uncut: uncut) }
213	        }

216	    /// Back on the main thread. Success is silent — the file is where the
217	    /// person put it — unless a cut-out clip was drawn whole because its
218	    /// masks were not ready (`uncut`, its media's file names; spec §11 CO-22
219	    /// (f)), which an informational sheet says; a failure is an alert on the
220	    /// window that asked. The whole path mutates nothing, so there is no undo
221	    /// step to group and none of `performGroupedEdit`'s off-event machinery
222	    /// applies.
223	    func frameSaved(
224	        _ result: Result<URL, Error>, in window: NSWindow, uncut: UncutFrameNote = UncutFrameNote()
225	    ) {
226	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else {
227	            if !uncut.isEmpty { showUncutFrameNote(uncut, in: window) }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        let alert = NSAlert(error: error)
231	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
232	    }

234	    /// What the sheet after a save that drew cut-out clips whole says (CO-22 (f)): the uncut
235	    /// clips' media file names, and the noun of their masks (CO-106).
236	    struct UncutFrameNote {
237	        var names: [String] = []
238	        var noun = "person masks"
239	        var isEmpty: Bool { names.isEmpty }
240	    }
241	
242	    /// The sheet after a save that drew cut-out clips whole (CO-22 (f)).
243	    private func showUncutFrameNote(_ note: UncutFrameNote, in window: NSWindow) {
244	        let alert = NSAlert()
245	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
246	        alert.messageText = "Saved without Remove Background"
247	        alert.informativeText = note.names.joined(separator: ", ")
248	            + " drawn whole: the \(note.noun) were not ready within 30 seconds."
249	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
250	    }

252	    /// The uncut clips' names for the sheet — each one's media file name, in order, each once —
253	    /// and the noun: "person masks" when no uncut clip is a foreground picture, "foreground
254	    /// masks" when every one is, "masks" otherwise (`CutoutWants.kind(of:)`, CO-106).
255	    private static func uncutNote(_ clips: [UInt32], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
256	        -> UncutFrameNote
257	    {
258	        let all = snapshot.clips + snapshot.nests.flatMap(\.clips)
259	        var note = UncutFrameNote()
260	        var foreground = 0, uncut = 0
261	        for id in clips {
262	            guard let clip = all.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else { continue }
263	            uncut += 1
264	            if CutoutWants.kind(of: clip) == .foreground { foreground += 1 }
265	            guard let name = snapshot.media(for: clip)?.name, !note.names.contains(name)
266	            else { continue }
267	            note.names.append(name)
268	        }
269	        if foreground > 0 { note.noun = foreground == uncut ? "foreground masks" : "masks" }
270	        return note
271	    }

276	    /// "not mine" and leaves the other answers alone — which is why the
277	    /// document is read INSIDE the arm rather than guarded ahead of the
278	    /// switch: an arm that answered `false` with no document would be
279	    /// answering for every other command in the chain as well.

457	/// One composed frame written to a file: a `CGImage` and a format in, a URL
458	/// out (road map 2 phase 7a).
459	///
460	/// It is `AudioNormalize.swift`'s shape applied to pictures, and it is a value
461	/// type for the same reason that one is. **File ▸ Save Frame… and the agent's
462	/// `render_frame` call this and nothing else**, so "Save Frame's PNG is
463	/// byte-identical to `render_frame`'s" is a fact about the code rather than a
464	/// claim in a comment — and it is the only way the line can ever be checked,
465	/// because a save panel cannot be driven over MCP or offscreen and a proof
466	/// script can therefore never press the menu item. Anything that goes in here
467	/// changes both paths at once; anything that lives in only one of them is a
468	/// place the two can drift.
469	///
470	/// So there is deliberately **no `NSSavePanel`, no `ProjectDocument` and no
471	/// AppKit view in this file**. Picking the URL is
472	/// `EditorViewController+SaveFrame.swift`'s job and naming a temporary file is
473	/// `AgentServer+Render.swift`'s; both hand the result here.
474	///
475	/// **PNG's properties dictionary is `nil`, and it must stay `nil`.** That is
476	/// what `render_frame` has always passed (`AgentServer+Render.swift`), and
477	/// every phase from 1 to 6 compares PNG bytes against frames written that
478	/// way. Anything that ADDS metadata changes the file: phase 7's proof
479	/// mutated this to `[kCGImagePropertyDPIWidth: 144]` and caught it by the
480	/// extra `pHYs` chunk.
481	///
482	/// The honest limit, measured rather than assumed, because the sentence
483	/// above invites a stronger claim than the platform supports: on macOS
484	/// 26.5.1 an EMPTY dictionary and no dictionary write byte-identical PNGs
485	/// (same sha256, same 5330 bytes, same chunk list, across two processes).
486	/// So no BYTE comparison can catch `[:]` here — but the rule is not
487	/// unguarded, and saying it was would send the next reader looking for a
488	/// check that exists: `phase7_chrome.py` reads `destinationProperties != nil`
489	/// STRUCTURALLY through the probe, which is what an empty dictionary fails
490	/// and a byte comparison cannot. That is a fact about this ImageIO, not a
491	/// licence — the rule stays `nil`, because the next ImageIO owes us nothing
492	/// and the failure would then arrive as a rendering change in five scripts
493	/// at once.
494	///
495	/// **JPEG flattens onto BLACK, and it says so out loud.** JPEG is the one of
496	/// the three containers that cannot carry an alpha channel at all, and phase
497	/// 7b makes a transparent canvas reachable in this very phase — so a person
498	/// who has just set the canvas to Transparent and saves a JPEG would otherwise
499	/// get whatever ImageIO happens to do with the premultiplied pixels, silently.
500	/// Black is the choice rather than white because black is what the preview
501	/// well and the exported movie already show behind the canvas: the still then
502	/// matches the picture the person was looking at when they asked for it. The
503	/// flatten belongs to JPEG ALONE — PNG and HEIC both carry alpha, so nothing
504	/// is thrown away in those two, and adding a flatten to them would destroy
505	/// information the format was chosen for. The panel's hint carries the same
506	/// sentence, because a silent flatten is the thing being avoided. JPEG is
507	/// also the one that holds 8 bits a component whatever it is handed, which is
508	/// why `Format.carriesDepth` is false for it alone and no frame grabbed for a
509	/// JPEG is read through the reader (spec §11 PR-9).
510	///
511	/// **The quality is 0.9, not `MediaImporter.writeJPEG`'s 0.7.** Those two
512	/// numbers answer different questions: a filmstrip thumbnail is 54 px tall and
513	/// is discarded when the cache is cleared, while this is a delivery still
514	/// somebody is about to put in a document. Neither number is a compromise
515	/// between the two, which is why they are written down separately rather than
516	/// shared through a constant.
517	enum FrameWriter {
518	
519	    // MARK: - The formats
520	
521	    /// The three containers Save Frame writes, each declaring everything that
522	    /// is true of it in ONE place: its type, the extension a file of it takes,
523	    /// what a menu calls it, and whether it can hold an alpha channel.
524	    ///
525	    /// The `rawValue` is a stable identifier for the agent's vocabulary and is
526	    /// deliberately NOT the file extension — JPEG's are "jpeg" and "jpg" and
527	    /// collapsing them would make one of the two wrong. `format(for:)` reads
528	    /// both spellings back.
529	    ///
530	    /// `UTType.heic` and not `public.heif`: only the former is in
531	    /// `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()` on macOS 15, so a destination
532	    /// created for the latter is nil and the write fails at the last moment
533	    /// with nothing to say. Measured, not assumed.
534	    enum Format: String, CaseIterable {
535	        case png
536	        case jpeg
537	        case heic
538	
539	        var contentType: UTType {
540	            switch self {
541	            case .png: return .png
542	            case .jpeg: return .jpeg
543	            case .heic: return .heic
544	            }
545	        }
546	
547	        /// The extension a file of this format takes. One spelling per
548	        /// format: the panel writes it, `destinationURL` replaces with it and
549	        /// `format(for:)` reads every accepted spelling back to it.
550	        var fileExtension: String {
551	            switch self {
552	            case .png: return "png"
553	            case .jpeg: return "jpg"
554	            case .heic: return "heic"
555	            }
556	        }

558	        /// Every spelling of this format's extension the app READS — one
559	        /// each, and JPEG's two, `fileExtension` first.
560	        ///
561	        /// It is the vocabulary and not just a list: `format(for:)` reads a
562	        /// name with it and the save panel's format popup decides with it

564	        /// is part of a name somebody typed. Those two questions have one
565	        /// answer and now have one home.
566	        var acceptedExtensions: [String] {
567	            switch self {
568	            case .png: return ["png"]
569	            case .jpeg: return ["jpg", "jpeg"]
570	            case .heic: return ["heic"]
571	            }
572	        }
573	
574	        /// What a popup row and a message call it.
575	        var displayName: String {
576	            switch self {
577	            case .png: return "PNG"
578	            case .jpeg: return "JPEG"
579	            case .heic: return "HEIC"
580	            }

content.content:
5 pages, 0 problems
docs site: 0 problems
52:| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or a lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox. 8-bit, always the SDR picture. Safari's transparent movie is HEVC with Alpha. |
289:- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** plays with its transparency in Chrome and Firefox, in a web page's `<video>`. Safari has not been confirmed to show it (see Limits). Only a player that decodes VP9 with the libvpx decoder shows the transparency; others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque.
290:- **HEVC with Alpha** is the transparent movie for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
310:- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
356:- Whether Safari shows VP9 with Alpha (WebM)'s transparency has not been confirmed; use HEVC with Alpha for Safari.
357:- A Mac with no encoder for a format reports "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." and leaves no file.
359:- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
365:- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

289:- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** plays with its transparency in Chrome and Firefox, in a web page's `<video>`. Safari has not been confirmed to show it (see Limits). Only a player that decodes VP9 with the libvpx decoder shows the transparency; others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque.
290:- **HEVC with Alpha** is the transparent movie for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
310:- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
356:- Whether Safari shows VP9 with Alpha (WebM)'s transparency has not been confirmed; use HEVC with Alpha for Safari.
357:- A Mac with no encoder for a format reports "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." and leaves no file.
359:- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
365:- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

docs/guide/mcp.md:306:| `format` | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. Wins over the path's extension, which is replaced. PNG and HEIC keep the canvas's transparency; JPEG flattens it onto black. | From the path, else PNG |
docs/guide/mcp.md:495:| `switch_by_speaker` | Cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** does, as one undo step "Switch by Speaker": a new track "Program" in front of the front-most camera (or `track`, an earlier one, replaced over the range), one piece per camera clip a shot crosses, the cameras hidden or their pictures off inside the range, and with `mute_cameras` their own sound off there; the microphones and everything outside the range untouched. Takes `speakers` (`[{mic, angle}]`), `wide`, `from`/`to`, `min_shot`, `min_turn`, `lead`, `crosstalk` (`wide` or `hold`), `bleed_db`, `dominance_db`, `wide_after`, `mute_cameras`, `track` and `apply` (false answers without editing), all optional. Works in the nest `set_scope` has open. Answers `applied`, `step`, `track`, `shots` (`[{angle, start, end}]`), `ops`, `added`, `speakers`, `wide`, `mute_cameras` and `mode` (`microphones`, or `faces` when one microphone is shared by two or more cameras and their faces decide who talks; then also a `note` that the cuts are a guess, and `min_shot` defaults to 3). In the faces mode it waits up to 60 s for faces still to be found, then is refused with what was found kept — call it again. Refused, naming every reason: under two cameras or over nine, a person without a microphone or a camera, one microphone for two people outside the faces mode, a microphone still being analysed or with no speech, a camera whose faces are still being found or show no readable mouth, a faces analysis that failed, was stopped or ran past the wait, a project changed while it waited, a stretch no camera covers, too many clips, a `track` that cannot take the shots, or a camera clip linked to its detached sound. |
docs/guide/export.md:251:| **JPEG** | None | A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. |
docs/guide/export.md:255:- Under the popup, a line says what the chosen format does with transparency: "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
docs/guide/export.md:363:- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
docs/guide/export.md:364:- The estimated time is the median of three measured exports per format and size, of real 4K camera footage on one idle Mac (an Apple M2 Max). On exports it was not fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time; a slower Mac, a busy one or a heavier timeline takes longer.
